---
title: "check-write-idiom.yml"
---

Diff-scoped, warn-only check that flags a line opening with
`Write the`, `Write a` or `Write an`.
In an exercise, "Write ..." means derive, express, state or give,
and the instruction should name the action literally
("Derive an expression for", "Express", "State", "Give").
This is [gha#1121](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1121),
from psw#297.

The check flags a line a pull request adds, in `.qmd` and `.md` files,
that begins, after optional whitespace,
an optional list marker (`-`, `*`, `1.`, `1)`)
and an optional label such as `(a)` or `a)`,
with `Write` followed by `the`, `a` or `an` (`Write` is case-sensitive).

The check does not flag:

- `Write $...$ for ...`, which is notation;
- `Write down`;
- `Write` anywhere but at the start of the line;
- a code fence or code span, an HTML comment, or YAML front matter;
- a line carrying, or following, `<!-- check-write-idiom: allow -->`.

## Scope

Only lines a pull request adds are reported,
so existing uses are not reflagged on every unrelated edit.
An added line whose exact text was also deleted in the same diff
counts as moved rather than new.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed
(a shallow clone, an unresolvable ref),
the check skips with a warning.
It never falls back to a whole-tree scan.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked file in full on purpose.

Every run prints how many lines and files it examined.

## Inputs

| Input            | Type    | Default | Description |
| ---------------- | ------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `globs`          | string  | `'*.qmd *.md'` | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore`   | string  | `''`    | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `fail`           | boolean | `false` | Fail the workflow when a vague `Write ...` line is found. Warn-only by default. |
| `whole-tree`     | boolean | `false` | Scan every tracked file in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string  | `'3.x'` | Python version to set up. |
| `runs-on` | string | `'ubuntu-latest'` | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository; never for a public one, whose pull requests can run arbitrary code on it ([#1167](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167)). |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-write-idiom.yml in your repo.
name: Check "Write ..." instructions

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-write-idiom.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   globs: '*.qmd *.md'                     # pathspecs to check (recursive)
    #   paths-ignore: 'chapters/outtakes/**'    # skip known-noisy paths
    #   fail: true                              # block instead of warn (defaults to false)
    #   whole-tree: true                        # scan every line, not just a PR's additions
    #   runs-on: private-runner                # self-hosted runner label (private repositories only)
```

See
[`examples/check-write-idiom.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-write-idiom.yml)
for the full caller stub.
